Hi Maya —

Thanks for the usage file — that helps a lot. Short answers up front, then options: 

Recommendation (quick):
- Start pilot on Dedicated with a small reserved pool sized for steady usage + a 30% burst buffer. This gives predictable p95 latency and the VPC/private deployment requirement.
- Use Redwood Console multi-region routing for APAC (primary in SG, fallback in hosted EU/US). For the strictest sub-100ms SLO, we recommend Dedicated in- region + KV prefix caching.

Tradeoffs and packaging: 
- Compact (hosted/metered): fastest to start, simplest billing, good for experimentation, but not ideal for private VPC or strict p95 SLOs at scale.
- Dedicated (reserved capacity): best for predictable latency and private deployments. Pricing is commitment-based; we can add an on-demand burst pool for seasonal peaks.
- Private (customer-managed on-prem/VPC): full control but longer lead time and ops handoff. We can offer Redwood-managed private control plane for a hybrid model.

Downgrade/proration model (how others typically handle it):
- Standard: quarterly true-ups with prorated credits for unused reserved capacity, 60-day notice for major capacity reductions.
- Concessions: 10–20% discount range for 12-mo commits depending on committed token volume; extra discounts tied to multi-year or enterprise-support add-on.

Next steps:
1) Quick 30-min packaging workshop — we'll map actual Q2 stats to a recommended reserved GPU count and burst pool.
2) I can circulate a pricing-sheet and an example concession matrix (see attached).

Looping Ben for capacity-side input and Lauren for pricing/concession authority. Happy to do the workshop this week.

Best,
Irene Choi
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Hi Maya — thanks for the clear asks and the LOI. Short commercial response and a suggested redline you can share with procurement: 

Commercial offer (summary):
- Product: Dedicated (reserved capacity) + Redwood-managed private control plane in your VPC.
- Commitment: 12 months. Baseline reserved pool sized for steady usage (est. steady tokens -> 2M/month) + 30% burst buffer.
- Discount: 15% off list for the first 12 months.
- Mid-term reduction: one allowable capacity reduction after month 6 with 60-day notice. Reduction triggers a prorated credit equal to 75% of the unused reserved fees for the remainder of the 12-mo term. (We'er proposing more conservative crediting to preserve capacity planning predictability.)
- Enterprise Support add-on: additional 5% discount if Clearline signs for enterprise support and a 24x7 on-call SRE engagement.
- SLA & failover: regional p95 SLA applies to Dedicated in-region. Cross-region failover to hosted reduces SLA priority and is classified as best-effort for p95 — we recommend dedicated in APAC if sub-100ms is non-negotiable.

Contract clause (sample language you can drop into the amendment):
"Customer may request a single reduction in Reserved Capacity once during the initial twelve (12) month term. Customer must provide sixty (60) days' prior written notice specifying the revised Reserved Capacity. Upon acceptance by Provider, Provider will credit Customer a prorated portion of the remaining Reserved Capacity fees equal to seventy-five percent (75%) of the unused fees for the remainder of the Term. Acceptance shall not be unreasonably withheld."

If that looks acceptable, we can:
- Run a packaging workshop to lock the exact reserved GPU count (Irene and Ben will size).
- Circulate a clean amendment + pricing schedule for signature.

I'll also flag this to Sales Ops for a quick one-time concession approval (DEAL-9821). Happy to jump on a short call to finalize.

Thanks,
Lauren Bishop
